A Family Kitchen Opens Its Doors for a Monthly Dinner
By Regina Toft
Nora Halverson, who runs the kitchen at her family's restaurant on Colton Road, has just launched a monthly evening for a handful of paying guests. Apart from this event, the restaurant continues to serve its full menu of simple home-style meals to local residents.
"Each month we set out one fixed menu of four courses," she says. "Guests sit around the counter to watch me cook every dish and listen while I explain what goes into it." The idea came from her regular customers. Some have eaten there since her parents opened the restaurant thirty-two years ago, and many kept asking to see how their favorite dishes were made.
Only ten seats are available each month, and places must be reserved ahead by telephoning the restaurant directly. A payment of forty dollars is taken at the time of booking, and the next evening will be held on the first Friday of April.

Nora Halverson, who runs the kitchen at her family's restaurant on Colton Road, has just launched a monthly evening for a handful of paying guests. Apart from this event, the restaurant continues to serve its full menu of simple home-style meals to local residents.

"Each month we set out one fixed menu of four courses," she says. "Guests sit around the counter to watch me cook every dish and listen while I explain what goes into it." The idea came from her regular customers. Some have eaten there since her parents opened the restaurant thirty-two years ago, and many kept asking to see how their favorite dishes were made.

Terrace Dining at The Sycamore Table
The terrace beside the main entrance is back in service for the warm season, from the first week of May until the end of September. During that time, food is served outdoors from 11:30 A.M. to 9:00 P.M. on every day the restaurant is open. The terrace tables stand under the trees and are screened from the street, and lap blankets are brought out on request when evenings turn cool. --[1]--.
What Is Served Outdoors
Terrace orders come from the same kitchen as the dining room, and the outdoor menu is drawn from the dining room menu rather than repeating it in full. Any item on it can also be packed to take home. Dishes are cooked to order, so a short wait is normal at busy times. --[2]--.
Finding a Seat
Terrace tables are not reserved. Reservations are taken only for the dining room indoors. --[3]--. Guests give their name to the host and are seated in order of arrival. Sixteen more seats will be added to the terrace once new planters and screens are installed, which is expected in late July. Each terrace table seats up to six guests. Groups of seven or more are asked to reserve a table in the dining room. --[4]--. Such groups are therefore encouraged to book several days ahead.
The Sycamore Table welcomes terrace guests throughout the season.

Business Services
Yardley Office Support Ends Charges for Repair Visits
By Theodore Sinclair
March 25
Yardley Office Support is replacing the fee it has charged office clients for each repair visit. Until now, the company has sent an invoice every time a technician was sent out. Under the new arrangement, clients instead register their individual machines with the company, and the number of machines a client registers decides how quickly the company responds when a problem is reported.
According to Vernon Middleton, the aim is to match the speed of service to how much a client depends on the company. "We wanted a simple and fair basis, one that ties our attention to how much equipment a client relies on us to look after," he said. Under the new terms, a client that registers five or more machines is promised same-day response, while a client with fewer than five is given next-day response.
Existing customers will be brought onto the new arrangement in stages over the next three months. Offices holding the largest service agreements will be switched over first, followed by the smaller ones, so that the company can confirm each client's registered machines before the old charges are removed from the account.

Evening League Adds a Third Division
Twenty-two teams entered the evening league at Riverbend Sports Center last spring, playing in just two divisions. Organizers say that arrangement put teams of very different sizes against one another, and several matches were settled long before the final minutes.
"A squad of ten was facing a squad of twenty, and neither side enjoyed it," said Beatrice Kowalski, the center's recreation programs manager.
Entries are therefore sorted this season by the number of players registered, with the largest squads placed in Division One and the smallest in Division Three. Division One plays on Tuesday evenings and the newly added Division Two on Wednesday evenings, while Division Three plays on Thursday evenings. Monday evenings are kept free for rescheduled games.
Entry forms are available at the front desk.
Clive Bannister, Community Affairs

Brindley Self Storage — Room to Grow, Whenever You Need It
Brindley Self Storage rents units to residential and commercial customers on flexible month-to-month terms, and every rental includes insurance for stored belongings and 24-hour gated access. Units range from a single walk-in locker to a space the size of a large garage. Prices rise with the size of the unit, and new customers pay only for the days left in their first month.
Visit any of our branches, where a site coordinator will help you choose a unit. Warren Bledsoe runs our Kirkby site, and Priya Naidu looks after Alderton. Geoffrey Talbot manages Roxton, while Lorraine Ackerman leads the team at Farndon.
Reserve online at www.brindleystorage.com or call 555-0173. Front desks are open daily from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m.
----------------------
Rating: 4 out of 5
Verified renter — Bethany Corliss, July 8
I signed up with Brindley after my spare room filled up with boxes. Reserving a unit through the website was simple. I had set aside my entire lunch break for it, but I was finished in under ten minutes. When I arrived, the site coordinator, Lorraine Ackerman, had my paperwork ready and walked me straight to my locker. My one regret is the size I settled on. Within a month my belongings no longer fit, and boxes began piling up at home again. Still, the staff have been consistently helpful, so I plan to keep renting here.
----------------------
Date: July 15
To: Bethany Corliss
From: Rosalind Tate
Subject: Your recent review
Dear Ms. Corliss,
Thank you for your honest review. I was sorry to learn that your rental has not worked out as you had hoped. Another renter is moving out of a space nearby that would suit your needs much better, and I would be glad to hold it for you at our standard rate for that size. Openings like this are usually taken quickly, so please reply by July 29 if you would like to go ahead. Any amount you have already paid for your current locker would be carried over to the new space.
Warm regards,
Rosalind Tate
Customer Relations, Brindley Self Storage

Trentham Library to Close for Roof Repairs
By Jonas Eckhart, The Vale Chronicle
The town's busiest library branch, Trentham, will close on Tuesday, March 1, and is expected to remain closed until early June.
Although the repairs were originally scheduled for next year, it was the discovery of water damage above the reading room that caused them to be
advanced
. The town council has also increased the funds set aside for the project, and the additional money will pay for a renovated reading room that, once the branch reopens, will accommodate more readers than the one at Rushden, currently the largest in town.
In the meantime, each of Trentham's services has been relocated to another branch. The branches taking them over include Wadebridge, the town's oldest library, and Blaxton, its newest, which opened only last year.
"For our members, it will be business as usual, just at a different address," said Deborah Guthrie, the town's head librarian. The Library Services Office has published a full list of the temporary arrangements.
